thesis: The guest explains that her academic focus on behavioral change originated from a personal struggle to balance academic work with exercise, leading her to realize that small behavioral decisions have massive cumulative impacts on outcomes like health and financial well-being. She describes how a specific graph showing that 40% of premature deaths are caused by changeable behaviors shifted her research focus from general behavioral science to specifically helping people overcome obstacles to making better decisions.
